answers.answer: Redis is a server program (a TCP daemon) that keeps data primarily in the computer's memory (the main goal is an in-memory database) and lets applications read and change it over a network connection by sending commands that act on abstract data types (strings, hashes, lists, sets, sorted sets, streams, vector sets, plus module types) stored under binary-safe keys. Writes can optionally be copied to disk files (RDB snapshots, AOF log) and to replicas. Problems it targets per the README: caching, session management, querying/sorting/analytics, messaging and interservice communication, vector operations; per type: counters, stacks/queues, unique-item tracking and set algebra, leaderboards and rate limiters, event sourcing/sensor monitoring/notifications, semantic similarity search and RAG.
answers.where: index.md, title block, Core ideas and data-types table; Advantages the maintainers state (use cases)

answers.answer: RDB snapshots dump the data set to disk (rdbSaveBackground forks a child that runs rdbSave), triggered by save points in serverCron or BGSAVE; the AOF logs write commands (feedAppendOnlyFile appends to aof_buf, flushAppendOnlyFile writes it from beforeSleep). Both can be on, or either off. Durability difference: with appendfsync always the AOF write reaches the file before the reply goes out; the full comparison of durability levels is not stated (the relevant redis.conf text is withheld). At startup loadDataFromDisk loads the AOF (loadAppendOnlyFiles) when AOF is enabled, otherwise the RDB (rdbLoad); a preload-file setting overrides both.

answers.answer: src/bio.c provides background worker threads that do background close(2), AOF fsync and lazy freeing off the main thread (lazy freeing only above LAZYFREE_THRESHOLD = 64, since small objects are faster to free directly). The ordering guarantee it gives: not stated.

answers.answer: Modules extend Redis functionality and let new commands be implemented rapidly (modules API); JSON, time series, probabilistic filters, t-digest and the Query Engine come from bundled modules. A module is a shared library named with loadmodule: at startup a loadmodule config line reaches queueLoadModule, and main calls moduleLoadFromQueue (outside Sentinel mode) after initServer and before initListeners. Bundled external modules are pinned in modules/modules.yaml, fetched with make modules-update, built by make, and configured via redis-full.conf generated by scripts/sync-redis-conf.sh; vector sets are an in-tree module. Loading into an already-running server at runtime and how a module data type is saved/restored: not stated (src/module.c is withheld).

answers.answer: The event loop (src/ae.c) is aeMain repeatedly calling aeProcessEvents, which waits for ready sockets with aeApiPoll (backed by evport, epoll, kqueue or select) and then runs file events and time events. The connection layer (src/socket.c) accepts sockets (connSocketAcceptHandler -> acceptCommonHandler); client handling (src/networking.c) creates a client with createClient, installing readQueryFromClient as the read handler, which reads into querybuf and calls processInputBuffer -> processCommand in src/server.c. One turn: beforeSleep runs (flushAppendOnlyFile, then handleClientsWithPendingWrites/writeToClient to send replies), aeApiPoll waits, afterSleep runs, ready file events fire (read handler before write handler unless AE_BARRIER inverts it), then time events such as serverCron (runs server.hz times per second: active expiry, rehashing, starting saves, replication reconnection).

answers.answer: Type is what a value is (an abstract data type such as list or set, defined by its operations and their complexity); encoding is how that value is represented in memory at the moment, e.g. strings as RAW, EMBSTR or INT, sets as INTSET or HT, lists as QUICKLIST (linked list of listpacks), streams as a radix tree of listpacks. Both exist because memory-saving encodings (listpack, intset) sit under each type for small values. Who decides which encoding is used (and the thresholds): not stated (the related redis.conf text is withheld).
answers.where: deep-dives/mechanism-deep-dive.md (memory-saving encodings); glossary.md (data-type, encoding, listpack, intset)

answers.answer: Clustering is split between src/cluster.c (maps keys to slots, routing: keyHashSlot, getNodeByQuery, clusterRedirectClient) and src/cluster_legacy.c (node failure detection via markNodeAsFailingIfNeeded, replica failover via clusterHandleSlaveFailover and clusterFailoverReplaceYourMaster), with slot definitions in src/cluster.h. A key's slot is the low 14 bits of crc16 of the key (16384 slots); if the key has a {...} hash tag only that part is hashed. processCommand calls getNodeByQuery to find the serving node; if it is this node the command runs, otherwise clusterRedirectClient replies MOVED (or ASK during a migration) with slot and address. Keys in different slots get CROSSSLOT; multi-key requests during migration can get TRYAGAIN.

answers.answer: connSocketAcceptHandler accepts the socket -> acceptCommonHandler (rejects if maxclients reached) -> createClient installs readQueryFromClient; clientAcceptHandler refuses non-loopback clients in protected mode when the default user has no password. When readable, readQueryFromClient reads into querybuf and calls processInputBuffer, which parses multibulk ('*') or inline protocol into a pendingCommand; on the main thread processCommandAndResetClient -> processCommand (I/O threads only flag and queue the client). processCommand looks up the command and gates it; then call runs c->cmd->proc (setCommand -> setGenericCommand -> setKeyByLink, server.dirty++, shared.ok). Because dirty changed, alsoPropagate queues it and propagateNow feeds feedAppendOnlyFile (aof_buf) and replicationFeedSlaves (multiple commands wrapped in MULTI/EXEC). Before the loop sleeps, beforeSleep runs flushAppendOnlyFile first (so with appendfsync always the write reaches the file before the reply), then handleClientsWithPendingWrites sends the reply. Checks that can stop it: authentication (noautherr), ACL (-NOPERM), cluster routing (MOVED/ASK redirect), memory (performEvictions fails and command is deny-on-memory-limit: OOM error), disk errors (writeCommandsDeniedByDiskError), read-only replica (roslaveerr), loading (loadingerr); plus maxclients and protected mode at connection time.
answers.where: index.md, Workflow 2 and table 'Main checks in processCommand'; deep-dives/mechanism-deep-dive.md (propagation)

answers.answer: When the AOF grows past auto-aof-rewrite-percentage and auto-aof-rewrite-min-size, serverCron calls rewriteAppendOnlyFileBackground, which forks a child. Further rewrite steps (how writes during the rewrite are captured, how the switch happens): not stated. File tracking: a manifest names which files are current: BASE (snapshot from the last rewrite, at most one), INCR (write commands since the last successful rewrite, possibly several, in order), HISTORY (what BASE and INCR become after a rewrite, removed automatically unless garbage collection is disabled).
answers.where: index.md, Workflow 3 'Compact the log', 'Life of the AOF files' diagram; deep-dives/mechanism-deep-dive.md (AOF lifecycle)

answers.answer: replicationCron sees REPL_STATE_CONNECT and calls connectWithMaster, installing syncWithMaster; the replica (slaveTryPartialResynchronization) sends PSYNC with a replication ID and offset. On the master, syncCommand calls masterTryPartialResynchronization, which accepts when the ID matches and the offset is still in the backlog, answering +CONTINUE (partial resync: only the missing data, then streaming). Otherwise it answers +FULLRESYNC, runs startBgsaveForReplication, and the replica receives the RDB in readSyncBulkPayload. In both cases replicationFeedSlaves then streams write commands; a replica passes its master's stream unchanged to its own replicas.

answers.answer: Two mechanisms: on access, expireIfNeeded (src/db.c) deletes an expired key on a master; activeExpireCycle (src/expire.c) scans in the background (serverCron includes active expiry). How the background cycle limits its own cost: not stated. Consistency: a replica does not expire keys itself but waits for the master, which sends synthesized DEL operations; replication and the AOF share one propagation feed. Explicit statement about AOF handling of expirations: not stated.

answers.answer: Stated design choice: a mostly single-threaded core, scaling by presenting many cores (on one or many machines) as one system through Redis Cluster. Extra threads/processes: I/O threads (src/iothread.c) read and parse but cannot run commands (they flag the client and queue it for the main thread); pub/sub, monitor, blocked and tracking clients stay on the main thread; new clients go to the I/O thread with fewest clients. bio worker threads do close(2), AOF fsync and lazy freeing. RDB saves and AOF rewrites run in forked child processes. Costs/conditions: io-threads does not parallelize command execution (an inferred throughput limit); TLS.md says multi-threaded I/O is not supported for TLS (possibly stale vs an iothread.c comment); helper threads start after modules load because of an ld.so TLS/dlopen race; lazy free only above a threshold of 64; forked children add copy-on-write memory pressure (no figure given). Why single-threaded execution was chosen beyond the scaling statement: not stated (manifesto quotations withheld).
answers.where: index.md, Core ideas ('One core runs commands'), Mechanisms table, Trade-offs; deep-dives/mechanism-deep-dive.md (threads); understanding.md u-choice-1/2

answers.answer: The sync-policy trade-off itself: not stated (redis.conf text withheld), apart from: with appendfsync always the write reaches the file before the reply goes out, and a failed write under always ends the process with exit(1) because the reply may already be buffered and the change cannot be rolled back. Why before sleep: flushAppendOnlyFile runs in beforeSleep before handleClientsWithPendingWrites so the log is written before replies are sent (AE_BARRIER exists for an fsync in beforeSleep that must precede replying); batching rationale beyond this: not stated. Durability given up during a background save with the mitigation on: not stated.

answers.answer: When maxmemory is set, processCommand calls performEvictions before running a command; it frees keys unless the policy forbids it. If it cannot free memory and the command is marked deny-on-memory-limit, the client gets an OOM error (shared.oomerr); otherwise the command runs. A 32-bit instance with no limit gets a 3 GB maxmemory with noeviction at startup. Forked children add copy-on-write memory pressure. Which memory or instances are exempt from the limit: not stated.
